dedupe_keys.name: characterization of the us industrial and commercial boiler population doe and ornl 2005

description: This report estimates the stock of industrial and commercial boilers in the United States by size, industry, fuel and region. The combined inventory holds about 163,000 boilers with 2.7 million MMBtu/hr of fuel input capacity: 43,000 industrial boilers with 1.6 million MMBtu/hr, averaging 36 MMBtu/hr, and 120,000 commercial boilers with 1.1 million MMBtu/hr, averaging 9.6 MMBtu/hr, plus an estimated 16,000 poorly characterised boilers in non-manufacturing industry. Industrial boilers are broken down for the food, paper, chemicals, refining and primary metals industries, and the appendices review source databases such as the Major Industrial Plant Database and EPA inventories. It was prepared in May 2005 by Energy and Environmental Analysis, Inc. for Oak Ridge National Laboratory with support from the U.S. Department of Energy. Coverage is national. The PDF is free to download from the Department of Energy; it carries the usual government disclaimer and no licence. Caveats: the data are two decades old, small units under 10 MMBtu/hr, over 70% of boilers, are least well documented, and figures are estimates built from several databases. For simulation it gives a baseline of the fuel-burning equipment that supplies process steam and heat, useful for industrial energy demand, fuel switching and electrification scenarios and for judging how gas supply interruptions would affect plants. It is related to the S&P Major Industrial Plant Database record in this catalogue, one of its sources.
